eintraege.titel: Eleven green months and the year still closes red.
eintraege.text:
Eleven green months and the year still closes red.

Plus 2 % a month for eleven months compounds to plus 24.3 %. Then one month gives back 30 %. The year ends at minus 13 %. Every one of those eleven months was real, and none of them said anything about the twelfth.

A smooth curve describes the months you have already seen. The one that breaks it has not happened yet.

Send this to the friend whose track record has no red months in it.

eintraege.titel: Six losses in a row is arithmetic.
eintraege.text:
Six losses in a row is arithmetic.

At a 50 % hit rate, six losses back to back has a 1 in 64 chance on any six trades. Over 200 trades you should expect that run to show up about three times. It is the coin doing what a coin does.

Most people rebuild the system after four. Write your worst expected run down before it arrives and it stops counting as evidence.

Send this to the friend who is rewriting his rules after a bad week.

What is the longest losing run you have had? 👇

eintraege.titel: A stop loss is an instruction. The fill is whatever comes next.
eintraege.text:
A stop loss is an instruction. The fill is whatever comes next.

The moment price touches your level it becomes a market order, and a market order takes the next available price. If the market opens below your stop, you fill at the open. A 2 % stop can settle as an 8 % loss across a weekend, and nothing about that is a malfunction.

The size of the position is the only part a gap cannot change.

Send this to the friend who holds through earnings because the stop will protect him.

Have you ever been filled far below your stop? 👇

Part 14 of the series.

eintraege.titel: Three positions at 2 % each is one bet at 6 %, if they all point the same way.
eintraege.text:
Three positions at 2 % each is one bet at 6 %, if they all point the same way.

The risk rule counts trades. The market counts direction. Three long tech names on the same morning move together when the morning turns, and the 2 % rule never saw it coming because it was busy counting to three.

Before you add the third one, ask what the first two already have in common.

Send this to the friend whose whole watchlist is one sector.

How many of your open positions would move together today? 👇

eintraege.titel: Test 20 settings and one of them will look brilliant by luck alone.
eintraege.text:
Test 20 settings and one of them will look brilliant by luck alone.

At a 5 % threshold, one false winner per 20 tests is the expected outcome. That is what the threshold means. The setting you kept is the one that fit the noise in your sample better than the others did, and noise does not repeat.

Run it on the years you never looked at. Whatever survives that was probably never about the settings.

eintraege.titel: A losing trade can still be the right trade.
eintraege.text:
A losing trade can still be the right trade.

A setup that wins 3 out of 10 at 3R pays 0.3 × 3 minus 0.7 × 1, so plus 0.2R every single time you take it. Seven of those ten will lose money. All ten were correct decisions, and the seven losers are what the edge costs.

The outcome grades the sample. The process grades the decision. Only one of those two is yours to set.

Send this to the friend who changes his rules after every red trade.

Do you grade your trades by the result or by the plan? 👇

Part 17 of the series.

eintraege.titel: Averaging down is a second decision about a trade you already got wrong.
eintraege.text:
Averaging down is a second decision about a trade you already got wrong.

100 shares at $50. It falls to $40, so you buy 100 more and your average is $45. Your loss is still $1,000, exactly what it was before you added. What changed is the money riding on the next move: $4,000 became $8,000.

The first decision was a trade. The second one was a bet that you were early rather than wrong.

Send this to the friend who calls it "building a position" on the way down.

Have you ever averaged down and been right? 👇

Part 18 of the series.

eintraege.titel: Your winners cost you more than your losers do.
eintraege.text:
Your winners cost you more than your losers do.

Say your average winner would run 2R if you let it, and you close it at 1R because green feels safer than right. That is 1R handed back every time you were correct. Forty winners in a hundred trades is 40R gone.

One losing trade costs you 1R. You count those. They are the smaller number.

Send this to the friend who takes profit the moment it turns green.

Where do you actually exit a winner? 👇

eintraege.titel: Every rule you added after a bad trade is still charging you rent.
eintraege.text:
Every rule you added after a bad trade is still charging you rent.

Five filters, each one throwing out a fifth of your setups, leaves you 33 % of the trades you started with. Each filter felt reasonable on the evening you added it, and every one of them was written by the version of you that had just lost.

If the edge lived in the whole set, you are running a third of it and wondering where it went.

Send this to the friend whose checklist grew after every red week.

How many rules did you add this year? 👇
